findings.description: For an existing, unexpired cookie, this now sends SetCookie, whose consumer calls wry's set_cookie, while delete_cookie still returns Ok. The cookie is re-set rather than removed; an app that logs out by deleting its authentication cookie therefore retains a usable session credential. Keep the clone removal but dispatch WebviewMessage::DeleteCookie(cookie.into_owned()).
findings.failureMode: An existing session cookie passed to delete_cookie remains active despite a successful result, defeating cookie-based logout/credential cleanup.
findings.title: Keep DeleteCookie when removing the clone

findings.description: The added extra spaces between these arguments fail the mandatory Rust formatting check. Running cargo fmt --all -- --check exits 1 and requests inner_size(size.width, size.height) on this changed line. Normalize the argument spacing.
findings.failureMode: The repository's required Rust formatting check rejects the changed inner_size call.
findings.title: Format the inner_size call with rustfmt

findings.description: The missing space after the comma independently fails the mandatory Rust formatting check. cargo fmt --all -- --check exits 1 and requests position(position.x, position.y) here; fixing only the inner_size line still leaves this violation. Normalize this call's argument spacing too.
findings.failureMode: The mandatory Rust formatting check rejects the position call even if the separate inner_size formatting defect is fixed.
findings.title: Format the position call with rustfmt

findings.description: Restoring tauri::webview::Cookie is a user-facing API fix, but this PR adds no covector markdown entry. The existing set-cookie and on_new_window change files are unchanged feature entries and do not record this restoration. Rule 13 requires a corresponding change file so the fix is included in release tracking and changelog generation; add one with the affected packages and appropriate bumps.
findings.failureMode: The public API restoration has no corresponding per-PR covector release record and is omitted from its release notes.
findings.title: Add a change file for the public API restoration

findings.description: The test renders GenericComponent<int>, but compares the marker's TypeName with GenericComponent<string>. Closed constructed types have different FullName values, so correct serializer output makes this test fail. Change the marker expectation to typeof(GenericComponent<int>).FullName.
findings.failureMode: Running CanPrerender_ClosedGenericComponent_ClientMode fails Assert.Equal when the WebAssembly marker identifies the actual GenericComponent<int> root.
findings.title: Assert the rendered generic type in the WebAssembly test

findings.description: Both markers are serialized with the same invocation sequence, which assigns consecutive values regardless of component type. The second descriptor therefore has Sequence == 1, not 0, and the new multi-marker test fails on valid output. Change this assertion to expect 1.
findings.failureMode: CanParseMultipleMarkersForClosedGenericComponents fails its final Assert.Equal on the second descriptor's sequence.
findings.title: Expect sequence one for the second generic marker

findings.description: The block-scoped namespace violates AGENTS.md rule 2 and produces IDE0161 under the repository's .editorconfig. Code-style verification with the exact-head test file fails at this declaration. Restore `namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.Circuits;` and remove the additional namespace braces.
findings.failureMode: Code-style validation reports IDE0161 for the newly block-scoped namespace; it no longer meets the mandatory file-scoped namespace rule.
findings.title: Keep the file-scoped namespace

findings.description: This new Task-returning method lacks the Async suffix required for all such methods by AGENTS.md rule 8. Rename it to CanRender_ClosedGenericComponentAsync to satisfy the mandatory naming contract.
findings.failureMode: The new Task-returning test declaration fails the repository's mandatory async-method naming requirement.
findings.title: Give the static-render async test an Async suffix

findings.description: This new Task-returning method lacks the Async suffix required for all such methods by AGENTS.md rule 8. Rename it to CanRender_ClosedGenericComponent_ServerModeAsync to satisfy the mandatory naming contract.
findings.failureMode: The new Task-returning server-mode test declaration fails the repository's mandatory async-method naming requirement.
findings.title: Give the server-render async test an Async suffix

findings.description: This new Task-returning method lacks the Async suffix required for all such methods by AGENTS.md rule 8. Rename it to CanPrerender_ClosedGenericComponent_ServerModeAsync to satisfy the mandatory naming contract.
findings.failureMode: The new Task-returning server-prerender test declaration fails the repository's mandatory async-method naming requirement.
findings.title: Give the server-prerender async test an Async suffix

findings.description: This new Task-returning method lacks the Async suffix required for all such methods by AGENTS.md rule 8. Rename it to CanPrerender_ClosedGenericComponent_ClientModeAsync to satisfy the mandatory naming contract.
findings.failureMode: The new Task-returning client-prerender test declaration fails the repository's mandatory async-method naming requirement.
findings.title: Give the client-prerender async test an Async suffix

findings.description: MainForm renders FormWrapper without openForm and sets isOpen when the editor gains focus or has content. Focusing the main comment box therefore throws reading in_reply_to_snippet and crashes the comments UI. Restore the deleted optional access (`!!openForm?.in_reply_to_snippet`).
findings.failureMode: Clicking or keyboard-focusing MainForm renders FormWrapper with isOpen=true and openForm=undefined, causing a TypeError and unmounting the comments UI.
findings.title: Guard openForm in the main comment form

findings.description: A signed-in member with a name but empty/null expertise now gets a read-only editor in comment, reply, and edit forms. Expertise is optional: the profile popup validates only the name. Restore the memberName check so these members can type without adding expertise.
findings.failureMode: A named member with null/empty expertise cannot type a comment, reply, or edit because setEditable(false) runs.
findings.title: Gate editor editability on the member name

findings.description: When replying to a reply, this form is rendered under the top-level comment, so parent.id is the thread root rather than the selected reply. The server discards that reference because it is not a child of the root, saving an ordinary reply with no reply-to snippet/link or notification to the selected reply's author. Restore openForm.in_reply_to_id and its callback dependency.
findings.failureMode: Replying to reply R in thread P sends in_reply_to_id=P. CommentsService rejects this as not a child of P and persists no in_reply_to reference, losing the selected-reply attribution and notification.
findings.title: Preserve the selected reply target

findings.description: Reordering this className to `pr-2 mt-[-16px]` puts padding before margin, contrary to the enabled error-level tailwindcss/classnames-order rule. The comments-ui lint target fails on this line. Restore `mt-[-16px] pr-2`.
findings.failureMode: Running the comments-ui ESLint target returns a classnames-order error at reply-form.tsx:47.
findings.title: Keep the required Tailwind class order

findings.description: This field pins the core tauri crate, not tauri-cli. The core manifest and lockfile remain at 2.9.2, but tauri init and tauri plugin init use this value to generate tauri = { version = "2.9.3" }. Those new projects cannot resolve dependencies while 2.9.2 is the latest core release, even though this PR only releases CLI/bundler packages. Keep tauri at 2.9.2 and bump only cli.js here.
findings.failureMode: Default app/plugin scaffolding after the CLI-only release requires tauri >=2.9.3, excluding the 2.9.2 core version actually provided by this repository/release and causing cargo dependency resolution failures until a later core release.
findings.title: Keep the core Tauri version pin at 2.9.2

findings.description: With either TAURI_BUNDLER_TOOLS_GITHUB_MIRROR_TEMPLATE or TAURI_BUNDLER_TOOLS_GITHUB_MIRROR set, this branch discards the resolved mirror URL and returns the original GitHub URL. download() requests that returned URL, so a clean-cache WiX/NSIS/AppImage build still contacts GitHub and fails on networks where only the mirror is reachable. Return alt_url instead of url.to_owned() to preserve both mirror options.
findings.failureMode: With a valid mirror setting, an uncached bundler tool download contacts blocked GitHub instead of the reachable configured mirror, failing bundling.
findings.title: Preserve the configured GitHub mirror URL

findings.description: `True` is not a JavaScript boolean literal and has no declaration. Both `tsc --noEmit` and the CI-configured `tsgo --noEmit` fail with TS2304 on this line, so the required Web Style type check fails. Return `true` instead.
findings.failureMode: Frontend TypeScript check fails on handleJSONSchemaChange with Cannot find name 'True'.
findings.title: Use the JavaScript boolean literal instead of `True`

findings.description: Clearing an existing JSON variable's schema now saves it without `json_schema`. The app validator leaves the input as text, and `StartNode` skips both validation and JSON parsing when the schema is absent. Running with `{"name":"Tom"}` therefore outputs a string instead of the previous object, breaking downstream object access. Keep JSON normalization independent of the optional schema so clearing it only disables validation.
findings.failureMode: Clear a schema in the console, save a json_object variable, then run with JSON object text: Start outputs a string instead of the object used by downstream nodes.
findings.title: Preserve object output when the optional schema is cleared

findings.description: A schema such as `{"type":"object","$ref":"#/definitions/v","definitions":{"v":{"type":"array"}}}` passes this check and backend schema validation. Draft7 ignores the `type` sibling of a root `$ref`, so input `[]` is accepted and emitted as a list for a variable advertised as Object; the old outer `type: 'object'` wrapper rejected it. Enforce an object constraint independently of the supplied schema.
findings.failureMode: A full schema with literal type object and root $ref to an array passes modal validation; Draft7 accepts array input and downstream consumers receive list for an Object variable.
findings.title: Preserve the object constraint for root `$ref` schemas

findings.description: Replacing the wrapper removes `properties: v`, the only use of `const v = JSON.parse(value)`. The replacement saves `value` directly, so the unchanged assignment is now a dead store. ESLint reports `sonarjs/no-dead-store` as an error at line 137, failing Web Style CI even after the other dead store is fixed. Call `JSON.parse(value)` without assigning its result.
findings.failureMode: Removing the parsed-value consumer leaves v unread and fails the mandatory ESLint check independently of normalizedJsonSchema.
findings.title: Preserve parsing without leaving its result unused

findings.description: `normalizedJsonSchema` is never read; `payloadToSave` repeats the normalization separately. Running ESLint reports `sonarjs/no-dead-store` as an error on this line, so the required Web Style job fails independently of the unused parsing result above. Remove this assignment and retain the normalization in `payloadToSave`.
findings.failureMode: pnpm run lint returns an error for the new normalizedJsonSchema dead store, failing Web Style CI.
findings.title: Remove the unused schema normalization assignment

findings.description: With the default global mock, `t('plans.community.features', { ns: 'billing', returnObjects: true })` now returns a string rather than the array the previous setup returned. Rendering the self-hosted plan List with this mock consequently throws `features.map is not a function`. Restore the returnObjects branch in the shared t factory so array-valued translations retain their shape.
findings.failureMode: Rendering web/app/components/billing/pricing/plans/self-hosted-plan-item/list/index.tsx using the default global mock crashes because features is a string.
findings.title: Preserve array results for returnObjects

findings.description: The setup now replaces real Trans with this mock, which ignores its components prop. A test rendering app/log/empty-element with initialized translations loses both shareLink/testLink anchors, so link assertions and interactions fail despite correct component code. Render the supplied component slots in the shared mock; the same scenario works with the base setup and real Trans.
findings.failureMode: A component which passes interactive elements to Trans via components loses those elements entirely under the new default global mock, unlike the prior real Trans and the documented mock contract.
findings.title: Preserve component slots in the shared Trans mock

findings.description: The old global useTranslation mock accepted a default namespace, but the replacement discards the hook's arguments and calls createTFunction without defaultNs. Thus `useTranslation('common').t('operation.yes')` returns `operation.yes` rather than `common.operation.yes`, and a namespaced custom translation cannot resolve through the hook. Accept defaultNs on useTranslation and pass it to createTFunction.
findings.failureMode: A supported useTranslation(namespace) call loses its default namespace, producing an unqualified fallback key or ignoring a provided namespaced translation.
findings.title: Forward the hook's default namespace

findings.description: The new interface violates the repository's mandatory type-alias rule and `ts/consistent-type-definitions: ['error', 'type']` in web/eslint.config.mjs, so linting the helper fails. Declare `type TranslationMap = Record<string, string | string[]>` instead.
findings.failureMode: Running the registered frontend lint check on the new helper produces an error for the interface declaration.
findings.title: Use a type alias for TranslationMap

findings.description: vitest.setup.ts does not mock marketplace/hooks or context/i18n. useMixedTranslation('en-US') still calls real getFixedT and returns 'All' for category.all, not a translation key; useGetLanguage still follows localeAtom rather than always returning en-US. Tests following this guidance can therefore assert the wrong output. Correct the claims here and at .claude/skills/frontend-testing/references/mocking.md:60–61 and .claude/skills/frontend-testing/assets/component-test.template.tsx:31.
findings.failureMode: Tests written according to the new global-mock guidance assert translation keys or an invariant en-US from hooks that actually execute real locale-dependent behavior.
findings.title: Document only the hooks actually mocked globally

findings.description: The public helper documentation says translations[key] wins over translations[ns.key], but createTFunction checks the namespaced entry first. With both `operation.yes` and `common.operation.yes` supplied, callers get the namespaced value, contrary to the advertised precedence. Update the comment to describe namespace-first lookup.
findings.failureMode: A caller supplying both scoped and unscoped overrides receives a different translation than the exported helper's documented precedence.
findings.title: Document the actual translation lookup order

findings.description: Replacing `export class SelectedCalendarRepository implements ISelectedCalendarRepository {` removes the symbol still imported by the subscription cron, webhook route and repository test. All 12 repository tests fail with `SelectedCalendarRepository is not a constructor`; both production routes construct the same missing export, breaking renewals and webhook processing. Update all consumer imports and construction sites to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository`.
findings.failureMode: The calendar subscription cron/webhook and repository tests import a no-longer-exported class, failing build/type checking and construction at runtime.
findings.title: Update consumers of the renamed repository export

findings.description: A matching calendar subscribed before deployment retains `syncToken` and `syncSubscribedAt`, but this filter now skips every renewal. After its watch channel expires, `CalendarCacheWrapper` still serves it from cache based solely on those two fields, so event additions or moves never reach slot availability. The visible cleanup only deletes past events; it does not reset subscription state. Clear cache eligibility for existing excluded calendars so their availability falls back to the live provider.
findings.failureMode: Deploy with an already-synced generic calendar; the new filter skips renewal after channel expiration while the cache wrapper still treats its old sync metadata as valid, returning stale busy times indefinitely.
findings.title: Invalidate existing cache eligibility when excluding calendars

findings.description: The exported class is now `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository`, but its file remains `SelectedCalendarRepository.ts`. This introduces a filename/class-name mismatch, which repository mandate 1 explicitly prohibits; merely changing consumers to the new symbol leaves that mismatch in place. Rename the module to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository.ts` and update its import paths.
findings.failureMode: The class rename introduces a new filename/class-name mismatch that fails the mandatory repository naming contract even if the missing-export consumer failures are fixed.
findings.title: Rename the repository file together with its class

findings.description: The added `vi.fn().mockReturnValue([...])` block is not in the form produced by the pinned Biome formatter. `biome format packages/features/calendar-subscription/lib/__tests__/CalendarSubscriptionService.test.ts` exits with a formatting error for this addition under the repository configuration, violating the mandatory Biome formatting rule. Run the project formatter on this block.
findings.failureMode: The mandated repository Biome format check fails on the new multiline mock chain in the service test.
findings.title: Format the new mock with the repository Biome config

findings.description: Adding Flatpak makes the exhaustive `From<BundleType> for PackageType` match in `crates/tauri-bundler/src/bundle/settings.rs:50` incomplete. Every tauri-bundler/tauri-cli build fails with E0004, independent of the user's target selection. Add the corresponding package type and conversion support when exposing this variant.
findings.failureMode: Compile tauri-bundler or tauri-cli: the match over BundleType fails because BundleType::Flatpak is not covered.
findings.title: Update the bundler conversion for the new Flatpak variant

findings.description: With `config-toml` enabled, `cargo check --locked -p tauri-utils --features config-toml,schema` fails with E0599 at this call: `custom` is provided by serde's error traits, not an inherent `serde_json::Error` method, and neither trait is imported in this module. This also blocks tauri-cli, which enables that feature. Import the required serde error trait before invoking its associated method.
findings.failureMode: cargo check -p tauri-utils --features config-toml fails on the newly added serde_json::Error::custom call.
findings.title: Import the trait required by Error::custom

findings.description: The parser now accepts `flatpak`, but `crates/tauri-cli/config.schema.json` and the generator's checked-in config schema still list only the previous seven targets. The CLI validates JSON/JSON5 against the embedded schema before deserializing, so `bundle.targets: ["flatpak"]` is rejected and startup exits. Regenerate the config schema artifacts alongside the new variant, as required by mandate 14.
findings.failureMode: CLI config loading rejects a lowercase flatpak target using the unchanged embedded BundleType schema, even though Deserialize accepts it.
findings.title: Regenerate the config schema for the new target

findings.description: BundleType's schema uses lowercase names but Serialize delegates to Display. A Flatpak target therefore serializes as `"Flatpak"` while its generated schema allows only `"flatpak"`, so serialized configs with this target fail schema validation. Return `"flatpak"` here, as for the other targets.
findings.failureMode: Serialize BundleTarget::One(BundleType::Flatpak) and validate against the generated BundleTarget schema: the uppercase value is rejected.
findings.title: Serialize Flatpak using the schema's lowercase spelling

findings.description: For a malformed `Tauri.toml`, this replaces `ConfigError::FormatToml` with `FormatJson`, so callers no longer receive the documented TOML error and the displayed diagnostic claims the file is JSON. The existing FormatToml variant still stores `toml::de::Error`; map the new parser's error into that variant rather than converting it to a JSON error.
findings.failureMode: parse_value on a directory containing invalid Tauri.toml returns FormatJson instead of FormatToml and reports the wrong file format.
findings.title: Preserve the TOML error variant for TOML parse failures

findings.description: This adds a user-facing configuration/API variant without any corresponding `.changes` file. Mandate 13 requires one for released functionality, and Covector generates the version/changelog update from those files, so the Flatpak addition will be absent from its release metadata. Add a change file naming tauri-utils and the appropriate bump.
findings.failureMode: Covector's next version PR has no change entry for this newly added configuration target because this PR adds no .changes markdown file.
findings.title: Add a change file for the new bundle target

findings.description: An alternative cluster implementation calling ASM_EVENT_IMPORT_START with `num_ranges == -2` now reaches `slotRangeArrayDup` before count validation. Its allocation size becomes 18446744073709551612 bytes and zmalloc aborts, whereas the base returned C_ERR for this input. Reject invalid raw counts before copying the caller's array.
findings.failureMode: Malformed slotRangeArray count supplied through the cluster ASM API can crash the server before validation runs.
findings.title: Reject invalid range counts before duplicating the array

findings.description: The added `total_ranges` variable is never read; the loop uses `slots->num_ranges` directly. `make REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror"` fails at this line with an unused-variable error, blocking the required CI builds. Remove the unused declaration.
findings.failureMode: The required warnings-as-errors build fails on asmCountKeysInSlots.
findings.title: Remove the unused key-count local

findings.description: For `CLUSTER MIGRATION IMPORT 8000 7000` or overlapping ranges, validation returns C_ERR, but `sdsfree(err)` replaces the deleted `addReplyErrorSds(c, err)` without sending a reply. Callers immediately return on NULL, so clients wait indefinitely and pipelined replies lose alignment. Restore the error reply; the existing input-validation test also times out on this path.
findings.failureMode: Invalid slot range command completes without any RESP reply; clients hang or associate the next command's reply with this command.
findings.title: Restore the validation error reply

findings.description: Normalizing before validating can erase a malformed range: `7000 7005 7006 7002` merges to `7000-7002`, so the subsequent start/end check passes and IMPORT starts a migration for a different subset instead of rejecting the reversed second range. Validate original ranges before any destructive merge.
findings.failureMode: A reversed adjacent slot range is accepted and causes an ASM operation on the wrong slot subset.
findings.title: Validate endpoints before merging ranges

findings.description: The count check precedes the new mutating normalization. With slots1 `{0-5,6-10}` and slots2 `{0-10,20-30}`, the initial counts match, slots1 shrinks to one range, and the loop compares just `0-10`, incorrectly returning equal despite the extra range in slots2. Move the count check after normalizing both arrays so range-array comparisons cannot falsely match different slot sets.
findings.failureMode: slotRangeArrayIsEqual returns 1 for different valid range arrays after only one array is merged.
findings.title: Compare range counts after normalization

findings.description: `asmCountKeysInSlots` is used only in cluster_asm.c and has no public declaration, but is added with external linkage (the compiled object exposes a global `T _asmCountKeysInSlots` symbol). This violates AGENTS.md's mandatory static-linkage rule for private helpers. Declare the function static to keep the implementation symbol local.
findings.failureMode: Private helper is exposed as a global symbol despite repository's mandatory static linkage rule.
findings.title: Give the new private counting helper static linkage

findings.description: Normal Razor accessors capture the page/model, but this process-wide dictionary strongly retains every distinct expression and only hot reload clears it. Repeated SSR requests or interactive rerenders therefore retain disposed pages and form models indefinitely. A GC probe retained all 1,000 models; repeated calls under a bounded heap terminated with 'Out of memory'. Cache model-independent metadata or use weak expression keys.
findings.failureMode: Repeated server-rendered DisplayName requests retain every captured page/model through static expression keys, causing unbounded memory growth and eventual process exhaustion.
findings.title: Avoid retaining accessor expressions in a static cache

findings.description: The added _displayNameCache is never used. The repository enables CA1823 and source-build analysis, and its build scripts default to treating warnings as errors. Compiling the exact new source with those settings reports CA1823 at this field and fails the build. Remove the unused cache.
findings.failureMode: Compiling Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web with repository analyzers reports the unused _displayNameCache field and rejects the build.
findings.title: Remove the unused display-name cache

findings.description: The new source file uses a block-scoped namespace, violating mandatory rule 2 and the enabled IDE0161 diagnostic. The repository runs code-style analysis during source builds and treats warnings as errors by default; compiling this file produces IDE0161 and fails. Convert it to a file-scoped namespace.
findings.failureMode: The new DisplayName.cs triggers IDE0161 under repository source-build settings and blocks warnings-as-errors compilation.
findings.title: Use the required file-scoped namespace

findings.description: When a parent reuses an accessor expression and changes CurrentUICulture, this reference-equality guard skips GetDisplayName and rendering. Resource-backed DisplayAttribute.GetName depends on the current culture, so the label stays in the old language after the parent rerenders. Reevaluate the display name on parameter updates (or include culture in the invalidation condition).
findings.failureMode: A cached For expression passed before and after a UI culture change leaves the DisplayName text in the previous culture.
findings.title: Refresh localized names when parameters are reapplied

findings.description: The default feature now pulls rustls-platform-verifier 0.3.4, which enables security-framework's OSX_10_14 feature and directly binds SecTrustEvaluateWithError. That symbol does not exist on macOS 10.13, still targeted by both CLI release workflows. A version check or tool download on 10.13 therefore hits a dyld missing-symbol crash. Use a verifier/dependency configuration retaining the older-OS fallback; tauri-bundler's default at crates/tauri-bundler/Cargo.toml:77 is affected too.
findings.failureMode: The released CLI/node binding on supported Intel macOS 10.13 references SecTrustEvaluateWithError absent from that OS, causing a dyld missing-symbol failure on load or HTTPS verification.
findings.title: Preserve macOS 10.13 compatibility

findings.description: With TAURI_BUNDLER_TOOLS_GITHUB_MIRROR set to a mirror prefix and no template, every GitHub tool URL now resolves to the mirror root instead of the asset. The deleted `cdn.set_path(github_url);` was the only operation preserving that URL, so downloads return an index page or 404 and hash verification/extraction fails. Restore that operation; it also eliminates the newly unused github_url parameter rejected by Clippy with -D warnings.
findings.failureMode: Base-mirror downloads lose the requested asset path and bundling fails. The deleted use also causes the required warnings-denied lint check to fail.
findings.title: Preserve the asset path in base mirror URLs

findings.description: `cargo check -p tauri-bundler --no-default-features --features platform-certs` fails with missing ureq::tls and tls_config errors: ureq/platform-verifier does not enable ureq's TLS API/backend. Make platform-certs enable the required rustls backend. The forwarding platform-certs feature in crates/tauri-cli/Cargo.toml:149 is affected too.
findings.failureMode: A no-default-features build selecting only platform-certs fails to compile because ureq's TLS config API is not enabled.
findings.title: Enable the TLS backend with platform-certs

findings.description: The new helper ends with `return agent;`, which triggers clippy::needless_return under the mandated `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`. Return `agent` as a tail expression so the required check passes.
findings.failureMode: The required Clippy check with warnings denied fails on the new helper.
findings.title: Remove the needless return rejected by Clippy

findings.description: With platform-certs enabled and a TLS interception CA installed only in the system store, the offlineInstaller HEAD uses base_ureq_agent and succeeds, but this new `ureq::get` uses WebPki roots. On an empty installer cache, the GET fails certificate validation and aborts NSIS/MSI bundling. Route the GET through `download(url)` again so it uses the configured verifier.
findings.failureMode: Building an NSIS/MSI bundle with an uncached WebView2 offline installer on a system-trusted private CA network fails in GET after HEAD succeeds.
findings.title: Use the configured agent for the offline installer GET

findings.description: When either GitHub mirror environment variable produces an alternative URL, this still returns the plain ureq::agent() created by generate_github_alternative_url, discarding base_ureq_agent's platform TLS configuration. A template mirror signed by a system-installed private CA still fails with UnknownIssuer with platform-certs enabled. Resolve the URL separately and use the configured agent for both paths.
findings.failureMode: Downloading bundler tools through a system-trusted HTTPS template mirror fails certificate validation even with the new feature enabled.
findings.title: Apply platform certificates to mirror downloads too

findings.description: Replacing `created_at:<...` with `<=` breaks the before-today query contract: the unchanged query assertion now fails on every run because `created_at:<=YYYY-MM-DD` does not contain the expected `created_at:<YYYY-MM-DD`. On MySQL, the inclusive comparison also admits newsletters created at today's midnight into the baseline for another send that day. Restore the strict `<` cutoff.
findings.failureMode: The query assertion fails for every invocation of the unit test; the generated MySQL query also includes the current day's exact-midnight datetime.
findings.title: Exclude today's emails from the warmup baseline

findings.description: Replacing `lastCount <= threshold.limit` with `<` advances exact boundary counts to the next multiplier: 1,000 yields 1,500 rather than 1,250, 5,000 yields 8,750 rather than 7,500, and 100,000 yields 200,000 rather than 175,000. The unit cases and integration helper require the inclusive ranges, so this also fails the unit suite. Restore `<=` for the tier comparison.
findings.failureMode: Prior CSD count exactly 1000, 5000 or 100000 and enough recipients produces an excessive warmup quota and assertion failures.
findings.title: Keep scaling thresholds inclusive

findings.description: With a previous CSD count of exactly 400,000 and enough recipients, this `>=` guard returns 475,000 instead of the 800,000 required by the inclusive 2× tier and the new progression case. Fixing the tier loop's `<` comparison alone does not fix this boundary; the progression test still fails at 400,000. Use `>` here so the high-volume cap applies only above the final tier.
findings.failureMode: A prior CSD count of exactly 400000 is routed to the high-volume cap rather than the expected inclusive final 2x tier, returning 475000 instead of 800000.
findings.title: Keep 400,000 in the final ordinary tier

findings.description: The new `count != null` violates the mandatory strict-equality rule and fails the configured `eqeqeq` lint check. ESLint on the changed files exits with “Expected '!==' and instead saw '!='” at this line. Use `count ?? 0` to preserve the null/undefined fallback without introducing loose equality.
findings.failureMode: ESLint exits 1 on changed DomainWarmingService.ts line 112 because of the newly introduced != operator.
findings.title: Avoid loose equality that breaks lint

findings.description: A proactive firing may have triggering_event=None. triggers.act now always supplies the emitted state-change event's UUID for normal automation.actions, so this validator raises ValidationError when constructing those actions and prevents publication. The state-change event exists independently of an original matching event; remove the requirement that triggering_event be present.
findings.failureMode: Valid proactive firing with no previous event publishes its automation.triggered state event then raises ValidationError in TriggeredAction construction; no actions publisher is opened or actions queued.
findings.title: Allow state-change links without an original event

findings.description: When an action raises ActionFailed, fail() constructs related_resources with triggering-event and automation-triggered-event entries but emits automation.action.triggered using only self._resulting_related_resources. The emitted event loses the existing triggering-event link and the new state-change link. Use related_resources here, as in succeed().
findings.failureMode: On ActionFailed, automation.action.triggered has neither parent-event related resource even with both IDs supplied; direct execution emitted zero related resources, while automation.action.failed and both success events contain the expected roles.
findings.title: Keep parent links on failed actions' triggered events

findings.description: For actions_on_trigger and actions_on_resolve, triggers.act supplies the automation state-change event as triggering_event, not the original external event. The new table therefore misidentifies what users will find via the triggering-event role for these actions. Document that this role points to the action's immediate source, which may be automation.triggered/resolved; the original event requires following the state event's links.
findings.failureMode: A reachable on-trigger action publishes a triggering-event link to its automation.triggered state event, not to the original custom event claimed by the table.
findings.title: Describe triggering-event as the action's immediate source

findings.description: The consumer awaits action.act before calling succeed/fail, which emit both action.triggered and the outcome event. A long-running action therefore emits no action.triggered event while running, contrary to this new statement. Describe it as a recorded trigger event emitted with the outcome, not a real-time start notification.
findings.failureMode: The new docs promise an event when an action starts, but during a blocked/long-running action the emitted-event count is zero; both action.triggered and the result event arrive only after act returns.
findings.title: Correct the action-start emission timing

findings.description: The new ReceivedEvent import is used exclusively in the parameter annotations at lines 314 and 417. Loading the test module nevertheless resolves it at runtime, contrary to AGENTS.md rule 2. Move this import into an if TYPE_CHECKING block and quote the two annotations.
findings.failureMode: The added module-scope import is exclusively for annotations and fails the explicit TYPE_CHECKING compliance criterion; the referenced class is eagerly resolved during test-module loading.
findings.title: Guard the new type-only event import

findings.description: If the billing API returns a tenant plan without expiration_date, this handler includes that tenant with a None value despite the dict[str, SubscriptionPlan] contract. The new test_get_plan_bulk_with_invalid_tenant_plan_skipped fails (three entries instead of two), and basedpyright also rejects this assignment. Skip the invalid tenant rather than inserting None, retaining the valid plans that follow it.
findings.failureMode: Malformed tenant plan produces an invalid None entry; the registered unit-test suite and Python Style type check fail deterministically.
findings.title: Skip invalid plans instead of returning None

findings.description: Adding __str__ to SubscriptionPlan makes the required basedpyright check fail with 'TypedDict classes can contain only type annotations'. TypedDict values remain plain dictionaries, so str(plan) does not use this method either. Remove the method from the schema and use a separate formatting helper if needed.
findings.failureMode: The changed declaration is invalid TypedDict syntax for static type checking, blocking the registered Python Style check on every run.
findings.title: Keep methods out of the TypedDict declaration

findings.description: When REDIS_USE_CLUSTERS is enabled, redis_client wraps RedisCluster, whose mget rejects keys in different hash slots. The generated keys for tenant-1 and tenant-2 occupy different slots, so even fully cached requests fall back to the billing API on every call; a billing outage then yields no plans despite valid cache entries. Batch GETs through a pipeline so cross-slot reads work on the supported cluster configuration.
findings.failureMode: A supported Redis Cluster configuration and a multi-tenant request spanning slots cause persistent MGET errors and bypass all populated cache entries.
findings.title: Use a cross-slot-safe cache read for Redis Cluster

findings.description: `TanStackDevtoolsWrapper` returns `JSX.Element`, so `lazy` infers that exact component type from the successful import. The new fallback returns `null`, making the import promise incompatible with the inferred component type. Both TypeScript 5.9.3 and the pinned `tsgo` report TS2322 on this loader, so the mandatory Web Style type-check job fails. Give `lazy` an explicit component type that permits null, such as `FC`.
findings.failureMode: The strict frontend TypeScript check fails with TS2322 because the import-failure default component returns null but the inferred lazy component returns JSX.Element.
findings.title: Widen the lazy component type for the null fallback

findings.description: In development with a non-English locale, a pending React Scan chunk displays the literal English `Loading devtools...` regardless of the selected language. Repository rule 11 requires all visible frontend strings to come from i18n, with no devtools exemption. Replace this literal with a translation key accessed through `useTranslation` and an explicit namespace.
findings.failureMode: The scan chunk loading state displays English rather than the selected locale because its visible string is not translated.
findings.title: Localize the devtools loading fallback

findings.description: For a fresh experiment suite that sets `jsonFileName` and `featureName` in the documented `setUpExperimentVariables()` hook, this reorder calls `setUpApp()` while both properties are nil. Passing them to the nonoptional String parameters of `addLaunchArgument` traps before the hook runs. Restore `setUpExperimentVariables()` before `setUpApp()`.
findings.failureMode: A FeatureFlaggedTestSuite subclass initialized via setUpExperimentVariables traps on implicit unwrapping of nil before its setup hook is called.
findings.title: Initialize experiment variables before configuring the app

findings.description: `BaseTestCase.setUp()` now throws, but the iPad-only override calls it with `await` and no `try`. Building the XCUITests target fails with 'call can throw but is not marked with try'. Use `try await super.setUp()` as in the iPhone-only override.
findings.failureMode: XCUITests compilation fails at the iPad-only setup call.
findings.title: Propagate the throwing iPad setup call

findings.description: The deleted block beginning `// This Source Code Form is subject to the terms of the Mozilla Public` is not replaced: the file now starts with `import XCTest`. Besides violating repository rule 1, this triggers an error from the enabled `file_header` rule, so the required lint workflow fails. Restore the standard MPL 2.0 block at the top of the file.
findings.failureMode: The required SwiftLint workflow fails on the mainline PR path because A11yUtils.swift lacks the mandatory MPL notice.
findings.title: Restore the MPL header required by SwiftLint

findings.description: Changing both fixtures to async leaves `forceRestartApp()` calling the inherited synchronous XCTest no-ops. AuthenticationTest's persistence check therefore never terminates or relaunches Firefox, and BookmarksTests relaunches without rebuilding its navigator. Migrate `forceRestartApp()` and its two test callers to async/throwing code and `try await` both setup and teardown.
findings.failureMode: AuthenticationTest.testBasicHTTPAuthenticationPromptVisibleAndLogin no longer terminates and relaunches Firefox during its persistence check; BookmarksTests.testLongTapRecentlySavedLink skips fixture reset.
findings.title: Keep explicit app restarts connected to the async fixtures

findings.description: Node-success layer callbacks run on GraphDispatcher, which does not copy the Flask application context. ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl resolves `db.engine` inside update(), so moving this call out of the context-preserving node worker makes ordinary conversation assignments raise `RuntimeError: Working outside of application context`. Pass an engine/session factory captured in the app runner to the updater (as the workflow repositories do), so writes can execute in the dispatcher thread.
findings.failureMode: Every real conversation update in the new layer fails accessing Flask-SQLAlchemy db.engine on a dispatcher thread without Flask app context; conversation values remain unchanged in the database.
findings.title: Resolve the database engine before entering the dispatcher

findings.description: Assigners inside an Iteration update a deep-copied pool, and their success events reach the parent before the child snapshot is synchronized. This line rereads the parent variable instead of `item.new_value`. With one iteration and a slow node after the assigner, the graph answers `new` and ends successfully, but the updater is called only with `old`; Iteration completion never triggers another write. Persist the value recorded in the success event while preserving the variable metadata.
findings.failureMode: Iteration child assignment succeeds but the top-level persistence layer saves an older parent variable, losing the last assigned value on the next conversation turn.
findings.title: Persist the event value, not the parent pool snapshot

findings.description: If update/commit fails (e.g. a missing variable row or a transient database error), the exception escapes on_event into EventManager._notify_layers, which only logs it. The assigner has already reported SUCCEEDED, so the graph continues and can report success while the variable is never saved. Previously the update ran inside the node and produced a failed node result. Handle the error here and fail/abort the run rather than leaving it to the layer exception logger.
findings.failureMode: A DB update failure is swallowed by layer notification; a successful workflow response loses the conversation state for the next turn instead of failing the node/run.
findings.title: Propagate conversation persistence failures to the run

findings.description: The deleted `with Session(db.engine) as session:` guaranteed rollback/close on all exits. The new Session is never closed: if the variable row is missing or commit/serialization fails, its SELECT transaction keeps the connection checked out until cyclic GC runs. Repeated failed updates can therefore cause pool timeouts in unrelated requests (verified with a one-connection QueuePool). Restore the context manager, as required by repository rule 6.
findings.failureMode: Missing conversation-variable rows or exceptions during update retain a transaction/connection instead of closing it; repeated calls exhaust the DB pool.
findings.title: Close the updater session on every exit

findings.description: The newly added __init__ omits its return annotation, failing AGENTS.md rule 1's mandatory explicit-annotation criterion for every Python function. Add `-> None` to this definition.
findings.failureMode: The new Python function fails the repository's mandatory explicit-return-annotation success criterion.
findings.title: Annotate the new constructor return type

findings.description: This new test is declared without `-> None`, failing repository rule 1's explicit return-annotation criterion for all Python function definitions; the rule does not exempt tests. Add the return annotation.
findings.failureMode: A newly introduced Python function fails the mandatory annotation criterion.
findings.title: Annotate the persistence test return type

findings.description: This new test lacks `-> None`, failing repository rule 1's explicit return-annotation criterion for all Python function definitions. Tests are not exempt from this rule. Add the return annotation.
findings.failureMode: A newly introduced Python function fails the mandatory annotation criterion.
findings.title: Annotate the missing-output test return type

findings.description: This new test lacks `-> None`, failing repository rule 1's explicit return-annotation criterion for all Python function definitions. Tests are not exempt from this rule. Add the return annotation.
findings.failureMode: A newly introduced Python function fails the mandatory annotation criterion.
findings.title: Annotate the non-assigner test return type

findings.description: This new test lacks `-> None`, failing repository rule 1's explicit return-annotation criterion for all Python function definitions. Tests are not exempt from this rule. Add the return annotation.
findings.failureMode: A newly introduced Python function fails the mandatory annotation criterion.
findings.title: Annotate the non-conversation test return type

findings.description: The newly added test lacks `-> None`, failing repository rule 1's explicit return-annotation criterion for all Python function definitions. The rule does not exempt tests. Add the return annotation.
findings.failureMode: A newly introduced Python function fails the mandatory annotation criterion.
findings.title: Annotate the factory test return type

findings.description: Standalone Xcode builds invoke `tauri ios xcode-script` from `src-tauri/gen/apple` with `TAURI_APP_PATH` unset. This new eager `resolve_dirs()` runs before `xcode_script::command` moves two directories up; its downward-only lookup cannot see the parent configuration and panics (reproduced with exit 101). Resolve paths for this branch only after its working-directory adjustment.
findings.failureMode: The generated standalone Xcode build script panics before compiling the Rust library because ios::command resolves directories while still in gen/apple.
findings.title: Defer path resolution until xcode-script changes directory

findings.description: When `bundle.windows.wix.fipsCompliant` is true and `TAURI_BUNDLER_WIX_FIPS_COMPLIANT` contains a non-Unicode value, `var_os` returns `Some` and this comparison silently changes the setting to false. The old `var(...).ok()` retained the configured value in that case. The bundler consequently omits `candle.exe -fips`, breaking FIPS-enforced MSI builds. Preserve the Unicode-validation fallback instead of treating an unreadable override as false.
findings.failureMode: A non-Unicode override disables a configured true FIPS setting and causes MSI generation without the required -fips flag on a FIPS-enforced Windows host.
findings.title: Preserve FIPS settings for unreadable environment overrides

findings.description: `dirs` is already `&Dirs`, so `&dirs` introduces `clippy::needless_borrow`. Clippy with `-D warnings` fails on macOS at this new argument, violating the required lint check. Pass `dirs` directly.
findings.failureMode: The repository-mandated Clippy check fails on macOS due to the newly introduced needless borrow in ios/build.rs.
findings.title: Pass the borrowed dirs directly to run_build

findings.description: `run_dev` already receives `dirs: &Dirs`; passing `&dirs` to `dev::setup` introduces `clippy::needless_borrow`. Clippy with `-D warnings` fails on macOS at this call. Pass `dirs` directly to satisfy the mandated lint check.
findings.failureMode: The repository-mandated Clippy check fails on macOS due to the newly introduced needless borrow in the dev setup call.
findings.title: Avoid the extra borrow when calling dev setup

findings.description: The final `mobile_dev` argument adds another reference to `dirs`, which is already `&Dirs`. This emits `clippy::needless_borrow` and fails the required warnings-denied Clippy check on macOS. Pass `dirs` without the extra `&`.
findings.failureMode: The repository-mandated Clippy check fails on macOS due to the newly introduced needless borrow in the mobile_dev call.
findings.title: Pass dirs directly to mobile_dev

findings.description: The inverted condition sends enabled/disabled updates to the repository without its required assignedBy value, and the inherit arm reads a property absent from that union member. Type checking reports TS2345/TS2339/TS2353, and the two new user-setter tests fail. At runtime a first explicit assignment also lacks the required UserFeatures.assignedBy field. Restore state === "inherit" so explicit updates use the attributed arm.
findings.failureMode: User feature assignments violate the repository union, failing type checking/tests and omitting a required database field.
findings.title: Restore the inherit branch in the user setter

findings.description: For an allowlisted user-scoped feature whose global flag is enabled, the new negation removes it from listForUser and the account Features page; globally disabled features are returned instead. Scope filtering should be added without reversing the existing global availability guard. Filter on state.globalEnabled, as the team/org listing still does.
findings.failureMode: User feature listing hides every available feature and lists globally disabled ones.
findings.title: Restore the globally-enabled user feature filter

findings.description: The deleted `await featureOptInService.setUserFeatureState(...)` lets setUserState return success before the write finishes and leaves rejections outside tRPC. Once an org/team-only feature is configured, its slug passes isOptInFeature but the new scope validation rejects; the client still receives success rather than BadRequest. Valid writes also race the client's immediate listForUser invalidation. Restore the await to propagate errors and finish persistence before replying.
findings.failureMode: User mutations report success for rejected updates and can refetch stale state before persistence completes.
findings.title: Await the user-state mutation

findings.description: UNUSED_CONSTANT is neither used nor exported. Running the configured staged Biome lint with --error-on-warnings on config.ts emits noUnusedVariables at line 5 and exits 1, blocking the normal pre-commit check. Remove this stray declaration.
findings.failureMode: The configured staged lint command fails on the new unused-variable warning.
findings.title: Remove the unused constant before staged linting

findings.description: A valid association such as {"ext":["png"]} leaves the optional name as None. Replacing `.unwrap_or(&association.ext[0].0)` with expect now panics during macOS bundling; every association in the example omits name. The CLI and SettingsBuilder pass the associations through without supplying a default. Restore the extension-based name fallback, handling an empty extension list without panicking.
findings.failureMode: Bundling on macOS crashes when a file association omits its optional name.
findings.title: Preserve the default file-association name

findings.description: For an extension-only association such as {"ext":["png"],"name":"PNG"}, the new is_empty guard omits CFBundleTypeExtensions and there is no LSItemContentTypes fallback. The resulting document declaration identifies no file types, so macOS does not register the configured association. Negate this guard so nonempty lists are written.
findings.failureMode: macOS application bundles lose every configured extension-only document association.
findings.title: Emit extensions for nonempty extension lists

findings.description: With exportedType.conformsTo=["public.json"] and no contentTypes, the generated UTExportedTypeDeclarations entry omits UTTypeConformsTo. If contentTypes instead contains the exported identifier, this code incorrectly makes the UTI conform to itself. Read exported_type.conforms_to here; content_types belongs only in LSItemContentTypes. Otherwise macOS cannot recognize the custom format through its configured conformance hierarchy.
findings.failureMode: Custom type declarations omit the configured conformance or substitute unrelated document handler types, producing an incorrect UTI declaration.
findings.title: Read exported-type conformance from conforms_to

findings.description: This new state is initialized to "" but setBookingUrl is never called, including in applyEventTypeData and the post-save refresh. Opening an existing event type with a valid API bookingUrl therefore makes Preview and Copy Link always show the save-first error; BasicsTab also always receives the non-org fallback. Populate the state whenever event data is applied, or derive it directly from eventTypeData.bookingUrl.
findings.failureMode: Existing event type detail cannot preview or copy its booking URL even after a successful fetch or save.
findings.title: Populate bookingUrl from fetched event data

findings.description: When the profile cache is empty and /me rejects, this catch replaces the original failure with a generic Error without a cause, code or request context. The detail screen's safeLogError then loses the original HTTP status/message and stack needed to diagnose the lookup. This violates the mandatory typed-error/context rule. Wrap the failure in a hierarchical typed error retaining its cause and request context; using the caught error also resolves the new noUnusedVariables lint failure.
findings.failureMode: Failed profile lookup produces an uncategorized diagnostic that loses the original status, message and stack.
findings.title: Preserve the username lookup error context

findings.description: The rewrapped Copy link assignment is not Biome-formatted: `biome format --line-width=110 companion/extension/entrypoints/content.ts` reports a formatting error at this assignment. This violates the mandatory formatting rule and fails format validation. Run Biome on this hunk before committing.
findings.failureMode: The changed Gmail Copy link assignment fails the repository's mandated Biome formatting validation.
findings.title: Format the Gmail URL assignment with Biome

findings.description: `scheduling.init()` forwards undefined options to post-scheduling, which still reads `options.apiUrl`. Every otherwise successful boot therefore rejects with a TypeError, and `bootGhost` shuts the server down before leaving maintenance mode. Restore `{apiUrl: urlUtils.urlFor('api', {type: 'admin'}, true)}`.
findings.failureMode: An otherwise healthy Ghost startup reaches scheduling.init with undefined options, throws while reading options.apiUrl, and exits via bootGhost's shutdown path.
findings.title: Restore the scheduling initializer's required API URL

findings.description: Deleting `slack.listen(),` removes the only production registration of the `post.published` and `slack.test` handlers. Sites with `slack_url` configured silently stop sending published-post and Admin test notifications. `slackNotifications.init()` only subscribes to milestone events and is not a replacement. Restore `slack.listen()` independently of the scheduling fix.
findings.failureMode: Even after the scheduling argument is restored, a clean process has no Slack post.published or slack.test listeners, so configured Slack integrations make no webhook requests on either supported path.
findings.title: Keep the Slack integration listeners registered

findings.description: The added comment tells contributors to use `npm install <package>`, violating the mandatory Yarn v1 dependency-management rule. This gives developers the wrong installation workflow for the Yarn workspace and lockfile used by the repository. Recommend `yarn workspace ghost add <package>` instead.
findings.failureMode: A developer following the newly added dependency-installation guidance is directed to npm rather than the repository's mandated Yarn v1 workspace workflow.
findings.title: Recommend Yarn for service dependencies

findings.description: When workspaceId and adminToken are configured, assigning tokenData makes getToken().token an object instead of a JWT string. The stats client interpolates it as Authorization: Bearer [object Object], so Tinybird requests fail authentication; the Admin token hook also rejects the object and disables analytics queries. Restore tokenData.token in _serverToken (which also lets the expiry checker reuse cached JWTs).
findings.failureMode: All JWT-enabled analytics calls fail authentication or are suppressed by the Admin hook due to the nested token object.
findings.title: Cache the JWT string rather than the token envelope

findings.description: Following the new setup instructions fails immediately: @tinybird/cli is not an npm package (the registry returns 404), so no tb CLI is installed. The repository provides yarn tb:install for Tinybird Forward; use that instead, which also satisfies the mandatory Yarn-v1 package-manager rule.
findings.failureMode: A developer following the newly documented local testing setup cannot install the CLI because the package does not exist.
findings.title: Use the existing Tinybird CLI installer

findings.description: The new local-testing command instructs contributors to run npm, although repository rule 23 requires all documented package operations, including run, to use Yarn v1. Following it uses the prohibited package manager. Change this command to yarn docker:dev:analytics.
findings.failureMode: The documented analytics startup procedure directs a contributor to violate the required Yarn-v1-only package workflow.
findings.title: Document analytics startup with Yarn v1

findings.description: `getRecordings` is async, so removing `await` puts a Promise in `data`, violating the output type and returning `{}` instead of recordings. Worse, an organizer requesting a booking without a Cal Video reference triggers the service's NotFoundException as an unhandled rejection, which can terminate the API process instead of returning 404. Restore the await.
findings.failureMode: An authorized organizer's recordings request for a non-Cal Video booking causes an unhandled NotFoundException rejection and terminates a default Node process; successful requests instead serialize data as {}.
findings.title: Await the recordings service result

findings.description: The added type-only import points to `@calcom/features/bookings/lib/BookingRepository`, but that module does not exist in this checkout. TypeScript still resolves unused type imports, so the platform-types build (and API dev:build) fails with TS2307. Remove the unused import.
findings.failureMode: Building @calcom/platform-types with tsc fails to resolve the newly imported BookingRepository module, preventing the API build from proceeding.
findings.title: Remove the unresolved BookingRepository import

findings.description: `BookingPbacGuard` requires `request.user` and throws UnauthorizedException if it is unset. It now runs before `ApiAuthGuard`, so a fresh transcript request with valid organizer credentials is rejected with 401 before authentication or the service runs. Use the same ApiAuthGuard-first order as recordings and conferencing sessions.
findings.failureMode: Valid authenticated organizers get 401 for GET /v2/bookings/:bookingUid/transcripts because PBAC runs before Passport populates request.user.
findings.title: Authenticate before the transcript PBAC guard

findings.description: Changing BOOKING_READ to BOOKING_WRITE makes PermissionsGuard reject an organizer's managed-user access token when its OAuth client has booking-read but not booking-write. This GET only reads recordings, and the parallel transcripts/conferencing GETs still require BOOKING_READ. Restore the read permission so read-only integrations keep access.
findings.failureMode: A booking organizer using a managed-user access token from a read-only OAuth client now receives 403 for the recordings GET despite having booking-read permission.
findings.title: Keep the read scope for fetching recordings

findings.description: The newly enabled recordings test calls `jest.spyOn`, contrary to the mandatory Vitest-only test contract. Vitest exposes `vi`, not `jest`, and the repository's Vitest setup supplies no Jest alias, so this mock fails with ReferenceError in the required framework. Import `vi` and use `vi.spyOn`.
findings.failureMode: The newly enabled recordings organizer test cannot execute its service mock under the mandated Vitest test framework because jest is undefined.
findings.title: Use Vitest for the recordings mock

findings.description: The newly enabled transcripts test calls `jest.spyOn`, contrary to the mandatory Vitest-only test contract. Vitest exposes `vi`, not `jest`, and the repository's Vitest setup supplies no Jest alias, so this mock fails with ReferenceError in the required framework. Import `vi` and use `vi.spyOn`.
findings.failureMode: The newly enabled transcripts organizer test cannot execute its service mock under the mandated Vitest test framework because jest is undefined.
findings.title: Use Vitest for the transcripts mock
